title: FDG PET Positivity Is Common Across the Clinical Spectrum of Well-Differentiated Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Tumors
content: Background/Objectives: The clinical significance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake in well-differentiated pulmonary neuroendocrine tumors (WD-PulNETs) remains uncertain. We evaluated FDG positivity in routine clinical practice. Methods: This multicenter retrospective cohort included histologically confirmed typical or atypical pulmonary carcinoids. FDG PET/CT was classified as positive or negative according to the original nuclear-medicine report. Results: Ninety-one patients were included; median age was 64 years, 69.7% were women, and among 81 patients with available histology, 67 (82.7%) had typical and 14 (17.3%) atypical carcinoids. FDG PET/CT was performed in 51 patients and was positive in 47 (92.2%). Positivity was similar in typical and atypical carcinoids (39/42 [92.9%] vs. 7/8 [87.5%]; p=0.514). Patients who underwent FDG PET/CT and those who did not were similar in age, sex, tumor size, histology, Ki-67, metastatic disease, subsequent metastases, treatment, and mortality. Surgery was more frequent among imaged patients (86.3% vs. 60.0%; p=0.013), whereas current/former smoking was less frequent (27.3% vs. 64.7%; p=0.015). Conclusions: FDG positivity was highly prevalent across WD-PulNETs and did not distinguish typical from atypical carcinoids. Binary positivity alone may have limited discriminatory value.
